This neuron has no clear lexical topic; it fires weakly on mid‑sentence continuation tokens — the infinitival "to" after verbs ("pleased to", "suspected to"), list-separating commas, digits inside dates, and rare word-pieces like " krat"(om) — and is most strongly suppressed at line-break "\n" tokens that start a new segment, so it appears to code "inside an ongoing clause" vs. "segment boundary."

L16·N6593unmasked layer
Fires at the token immediately preceding a literal identifier/code string — e.g. "by"/"Published" before a publisher name, the separator/digit before a UPC, part number, PCI\VEN_ hardware ID, or obfuscated email ("[dot]") — i.e. the cue that a machine-readable code or attribution string follows; it is strongly suppressed on the final subword of brand/proper-name compounds (AccessPress, Wigwam, SASS, Ink361).
